items.title: AP investigation: 3+ dozen new voting laws taking effect this year in GOP states, many mirroring Trump's stalled federal proposals
items.summary: An AP investigation by Gary Fields and Julie Carr Smyth (published Mon, Oct 12) found more than three dozen voting laws passed in Republican-controlled states taking effect for the first time this year: tougher voter-ID rules, proof-of-citizenship requirements, stricter mail-in ballot deadlines and new voter-roll maintenance procedures. Trump's federal pushes (proof-of-citizenship law, national voter-ID executive order, USPS mail-voting limits) failed to clear Congress/courts in time; conservative state legislatures advanced their own versions. Brennan Center identified nearly 40 laws in 21 states that make it harder for eligible voters to register, stay on the rolls or cast ballots; supporters call them common-sense safeguards.
